# An exact obstruction to a parity-efficient ell-contact cell cover

The proposed subdivision statement is false under its stated finite
hypotheses. The example has a lattice-complete two-dimensional base,
positive concave ell, a closed source minor J on which every anchored
relation has ell equality, and an ell-tight martingale with a strictly
positive target on EVERY base. Nevertheless the least possible sum of
occupied parity counts of the permitted contact-cell minors is EIGHT,
whereas the original base occupies only FOUR parities.

Section 4 additionally realizes the target as the exact inverse-ell tilted
volumes of an actual compatible three-dimensional homothetic family.
Section 5 records its failed singleton quota. The stronger Section 6 then
gives a completely RATIONAL canonical interval family satisfying ALL
strict proper closed-minor quotas and the same exact transport and parity
obstruction. No assertion that J is a deepest set is made for either family.

## 1. Finite base, concave roof, and source minor

Let

    P={-1,0,1,2} times {-1,0,1} subset Z^2,
    q(x,y)=2x+y-1,
    ell(x,y)=5-|q(x,y)|,
    J={p_0=(0,0),p_1=(1,0)}.                              (1)

P is exactly the integer points of the rectangle B=[-1,2] times [-1,1].
It is full-dimensional in the inherited lattice Z^2 and has k(P)=4.
On B, |q|<=4, so ell>=1. It is a genuine positive continuous concave
piecewise-affine roof, not just positive sampled values.

The two roof facets project to

    B_-={z in B:q(z)<=0},      B_+={z in B:q(z)>=0},
    ell_-(x,y)=4+2x+y,        ell_+(x,y)=6-2x-y.           (2)

Their common edge has endpoints (0,1),(1,-1), both in P. The source p_0
lies in relint B_- and p_1 in relint B_+. Thus the MINIMAL upper-roof
face containing each lifted source is precisely its respective full
facet. In particular no larger single upper face contains both sources.

J=P intersect conv(J): its segment is primitive and contains no other
integer point. An anchored representation of either endpoint by points
of J is necessarily the identity. Hence ell equality holds for EVERY
anchored relation entirely within J. This hypothesis does not say that
ell is affine along the whole real segment between the two endpoints:
its midpoint has ell=5, whereas the two endpoints have ell=4.

## 2. A completely rational positive-target martingale

Inject unit mass at each source p_0,p_1. The conditional target weights
from p_0 are the following numerators divided by 12:

| target z | (-1,-1) | (-1,0) | (-1,1) | (0,-1) | (0,0) | (0,1) | (1,-1) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| numerator | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 4 | 3 |

They sum to 12, have x-moment -3+3=0, and y-moment
-1+1-1+4-3=0. Every target lies in B_-, where ell is affine, so their
ell mean is exactly ell(p_0)=4.

Define the second row by the exact reflection

    R(x,y)=(1-x,-y).                                      (3)

It exchanges the two facets and the two sources, preserves P and ell,
and makes the second row have mean p_1 and ell mean 4. The combined
target nu is strictly positive on every point of P: it has mass 7/12
at each crease point (0,1),(1,-1), and 1/12 at each of the other ten
points. Its total mass is 2. This is an exact ell-tight martingale from
mu=delta_(p_0)+delta_(p_1), with no vanishing target coordinates or
unproved source injection.

## 3. Every allowed contact-cell cover costs at least eight parities

Consider ANY finite cover P=union_c T_c in which each T_c is a closed
minor, ell is affine on its supporting contact cell, and T_c lies in a
minimal upper-roof face of some source in J. Necessarily every T_c lies
wholly in B_- or wholly in B_+. No one such cell can contain a point with
q<0 and another with q>0.

All four parity classes occur on EACH strict side. Explicit representatives
are

| parity (x mod 2,y mod 2) | strict B_- point | strict B_+ point |
|---|---|---|
| (0,0) | (0,0) | (2,0) |
| (0,1) | (0,-1) | (2,-1) |
| (1,0) | (-1,0) | (1,0) |
| (1,1) | (-1,1) | (1,1) |

For each parity, its two displayed representatives must therefore be
covered by at least two DISTINCT cells. Counting occurrences of parity
classes across the cover gives

    sum_c k(T_c)>=2+2+2+2=8>4=k(P).                      (4)

This lower bound is attained. The two actual facet minors

    T_-=P intersect B_-,      T_+=P intersect B_+

are closed minors because all four vertices of either B facet polygon
belong to P. Each has k=4, and they cover P. Thus the exact minimum
contact-cell parity cost is 8, not merely some lower bound above 4.
The failure cannot be fixed by choosing smaller cells or singleton cells.
It is repeated TARGET parities across distinct contact facets, not a
failure of the source martingale or of closed-minor completeness.

## 4. A canonical actual family with the exact V/ell target

The preceding rational certificate suffices to refute the stated finite
claim. The following stronger construction shows that its target can
also have the exact tilted-volume form arising in the multiplier theorem.

Let R_0 be the unique root in (4,5) of

    67 R_0^3-735 R_0^2+2685 R_0-3365=0.                 (5)

Existence follows from the polynomial values -97 at 4 and 60 at 5.
Its derivative is positive throughout [4,5]: the derivative equals 21
at 4 and its own derivative 402R-1470 is positive there. Thus the root
is unique and all constants below are exact real algebraic numbers.

Take continuous dimension d=3 and the unit-volume cube
D=[-1/2,1/2]^3. Define actual fibers by

    r(z)=R_0-|q(z)|>0,
    K_z=r(z)D,          V_z=r(z)^3.                      (6)

The radius is concave and positive on the entire rectangle, so these
fibers obey every anchored Minkowski inclusion. The actual convex body

    C={(z,X):z in B, X in r(z)D}

is CANONICAL: on each B facet polygon the radius is affine and all its
vertices lie in P. Every real-base fiber is the Minkowski interpolation
of those sampled vertex fibers. Hence C is exactly the convex hull of
the sampled fibers, and its integer bases are exactly P. No noninteger
fiber is silently substituted into the mixed family.

Write

    a=(R_0-4)^3,
    b=(R_0-3)^3/2,
    c=(R_0-2)^3/3,
    d_0=(R_0-1)^3/4,
    g=R_0^3/5.                                           (7)

All are strictly positive. Equation (5) is exactly the identity

    g=3a+2b+2c.                                         (8)

The desired target nu_z=V_z/ell_z has values a,b,c,c,d_0 on the five
strict left points in the table of Section 2, and g on each crease point;
the strict right values are their reflections.

Give the p_0 row the following UNNORMALIZED weights on the same seven
points as that table:

    a, b, c, c, d_0, 2a+b+c, a+b+c.                      (9)

Its total mass is m_0=4a+3b+4c+d_0. Its x-moment is
-(a+b+c)+(a+b+c)=0, and its y-moment is
-a+c-c+(2a+b+c)-(a+b+c)=0. Reflect the row to p_1 as before. At each
crease point the two rows sum to (2a+b+c)+(a+b+c)=g by (8). Every other
column is its prescribed target value. Thus these rows give an exact
martingale

    m_0 delta_(p_0)+m_0 delta_(p_1) --> sum_z V_z/ell_z delta_z,

with full positive target and ell mean preserved at each source.
Because the source ell values are 4, the actual total volume is

    M=sum V_z=8m_0.                                     (10)

Consequently the target equals Delta sum w_z/ell_z delta_z with
Delta=M and w_z=V_z/M, exactly the volume-martingale normalization.
Scaling ell by its positive geometric-mean normalization scalar and
scaling both transport marginals inversely preserves every assertion.

These are actual compatible positive fibers and exact volume marginals.
We do NOT assert that J is a deepest set, that the coefficients arise
from an actual critical response, or that this family is a bad minimum.
The precise finite hypotheses of the proposed cover statement, even
with an actual tilted-volume target, are what have been realized.

## 5. The actual-volume realization fails a strict minor quota

A cheap exact check avoids any large closed-minor enumeration. The root
in (5) lies in

    24/5<R_0<481/100,

because the corresponding polynomial values are -217/125 and
887447/1000000. At either crease base the volume is V_crease=R_0^3.
Using (8)--(10), its excess over the singleton quota M/k(P)=M/4 is

    V_crease-M/4=7a+4b+2c-2d_0
      >7(4/5)^3+2(9/5)^3+(2/3)(14/5)^3-(1/2)(381/100)^3
      =13376977/6000000>0.                              (11)

Thus this three-dimensional actual-volume version does not satisfy all
strict closed-minor quotas. The next construction answers the distinct
quota-constrained question, also with actual compatible fibers.

## 6. Rational interval fibers satisfy every strict minor quota

Keep precisely P,ell,J from (1). In lexicographic order of P, take the
following positive fiber lengths, all divided by 1230:

    (2,2,2,136,203,270,270,203,136,2,2,2).                (12)

Their sum is M=1. Define a real-base length roof by

    V(x,y)=min{270+67q,270-67q,270+268x,538-268x}/1230.    (13)

It is concave as the minimum of four affine functions, equals (12) at
all sampled bases, and is everywhere at least 2/1230 on B. Centered
interval fibers K_z=[-V(z)/2,V(z)/2] are therefore genuinely compatible
in continuous dimension d=1, not just abstract positive mass assignments.

Their convex hull is canonical. The four roof pieces are the triangles

    conv{(-1,-1),(-1,1),(0,1)},
    conv{(-1,-1),(0,1),(1,-1)},
    conv{(0,1),(1,-1),(2,1)},
    conv{(1,-1),(2,-1),(2,1)}.                           (14)

They tile the rectangle, their vertices all belong to P, and V is affine
on each with the corresponding plane in (13). Hence every real fiber
is exactly a Minkowski interpolation of sampled vertex intervals. The
body {(z,X):z in B,|X|<=V(z)/2} is precisely the sampled convex hull.

The exact ell-tight martingale is again explicit. On the same ordered
seven left targets used in Section 2, give the source p_0 the following
UNNORMALIZED weights divided by 14760:

    (24,12,8,544,609,604,44).                             (15)

They sum to 1845/14760=1/8, and their x- and y-moments vanish. Reflect
this row by (3) for p_1. The two rows combined have target exactly

    nu_z=V_z/ell_z>0,
    mu=(delta_(p_0)+delta_(p_1))/8.                       (16)

For example, each crease receives (604+44)/14760=9/205,
which equals its volume (270/1230) divided by ell=5. Every other point
is reached by just the one appropriate strict-side row. The mean of ell
is preserved at each source because its whole row lies in one affine
roof facet. Since M=1 and source ell is 4, Delta=1 gives exactly
nu=Delta sum w_z/ell_z delta_z. Geometric normalization of ell, if desired,
is the harmless positive rescaling described in Section 4.

Here EVERY proper closed minor has a strict parity quota

    V_T<k(T)M/k(P)=k(T)/4.                              (17)

This is a finite exact certificate, verified exhaustively as follows.
Enumerate all 4094 nonempty proper subsets of the twelve explicit integer
points. For each subset S take its exact integer convex hull, including
the segment and singleton cases, and retain it iff P intersect conv(S)=S.
There are exactly 704 retained closed minors. Using integer length
numerators n_z from (12), check

    1230 k(S)-4 sum_(z in S)n_z>0                        (18)

for every retained S. The complete code is in the companion verifier;
it uses integer cross products and exact rational arithmetic only.
Consequently (17) is not a floating LP inference. In particular no
proper minor or lower-dimensional subset is omitted.

For k(S)=1,2,3,4 respectively, the least strict quota margins are
(150,24,166,8)/4920. The complete companion
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_ell_contact_cell_parity_obstruction_defect_transport.py` passes
1,536 exact checks, including both target flows, canonicality of the
four-plane interval roof, and all 704 quotas for this final certificate.

The same two ell-contact facets and parity table in Section 3 remain
unchanged. Therefore even with this actual canonical convex family,
strictly positive fibers, exact V/ell target, and ALL strict minor quotas,
the minimal permitted contact-cell cover cost is still 8>k(P)=4.

The missing hypothesis cannot be repaired merely by radius concavity,
Brunn--Minkowski compatibility, or strict mass quotas. The source set J
is NOT asserted to consist of actual deepest marks for this family, and
no critical cap or below-target claim is supplied. Any stronger theorem
using such additional geometric data would need a genuinely new premise.
